title: Templated Incident Narratives and Runbook Modules
author: Aisha K. Morales
content:
Overview
---
This page defines a modular approach to incident runbooks and a library of templated incident narratives, postmortem scaffolds, on-call handoff checklists, game-day exercises, and staged customer status messages. The goal is to reduce time-to-stabilize, standardize external communication, and make post-incident learning actionable across teams.

Scope and intent
---
- Scope: LLM serving, control plane, routing/fallbacks, and customer-visible outages for Redwood Inference.
- Intent: Provide ready-to-use runbook modules that responders can copy/paste and adapt during an incident. Include narrative templates for quick customer-facing updates. Ensure every incident produces a reproducible investigation and ownerable follow-ups.

Audience
---
- Primary: SREs, on-call engineers, incident commanders.
- Secondary: Product engineering, customer success, account managers, and leadership who approve customer comms.

Quick reference: escalation tiers and SLAs
---
| Tier | Symptom examples | Time to initial acknowledge | Escalation path |
|------|------------------|----------------------------:|----------------|
| P0 | Total region outage, API returns 50s for majority of requests | 1 minute | Pager -> primary oncall -> IC -> Eng lead -> Exec oncall |
| P1 | Severe latency degradation causing SLO breach > 30 min | 5 minutes | Pager -> primary oncall -> Eng lead -> Customer success notify |
| P2 | Feature regressions (model quality, embeddings mismatch) | 30 minutes | Slack alert -> owner -> triage meeting |

Incident lifecycle (high-level)
---
1. Detection and acknowledgement: follow signal catalog (see appendix). Annotate initial evidence (metrics links, traces, sample request IDs).
2. Triage: determine impact (customers, regions, model variants), classify Tier.
3. Containment: apply fallbacks (route to warm model variant, throttle/queue, enable degraded mode), document actions with timestamps.
4. Restoration: scale up capacity, run targeted remediation, monitor SLO recovery.
5. Communicate: status page update cadence + customer-notice templates.
6. Post-incident: snapshot evidence, collect debug artifacts, publish postmortem within 72 hours (draft) and final within 14 days.

Runbook modules (copyable blocks)
---
Each module is a short, repeatable set of steps the responder can paste into the incident timeline. Replace bracketed fields.

Module: Collect primary evidence
- Step 1: Open metrics dashboards: Token throughput (serving/token-sla), request error rate (gateway/errors), p50/p95/p99 latency for model <MODEL_ID>.
- Step 2: Run sample queries: curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"model":"<MODEL_ID>","input":"<SMOKE_INPUT>"}' and capture request ID.
- Step 3: Attach logs/traces: kubectl logs -l service=<SERVICE> --since=10m > /tmp/logs.txt; upload to incident artifact store.

Module: Apply immediate fallback routing
- Preconditions: alternate compatible model variant exists (e.g., <MODEL_ID>-quant8-warm) and warm pool available.
- Steps: 
  1) Update routing policy in control-plane: POST /internal/routing -d '{"from":"<MODEL_ID>","to":"<FALLBACK_MODEL>","pct":100}'
  2) Verify: run 10 quick requests and confirm responses within SLO.
  3) Monitor for 15 minutes for error decrease.

Module: Throttle noisy tenants
- Steps: Identify top 5 tenants by QPS using query: SELECT tenant_id, sum(qps) FROM requests WHERE window=5m GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY sum(qps) DESC LIMIT 5; apply rate-limit policy per-tenant via admin UI or API.

Postmortem skeleton (90-min draft template)
---
Use this to produce an initial postmortem draft for review. Replace placeholders.
1) Summary: one-paragraph timeline and customer impact.
2) Components affected: list services and models.
3) Timeline: bulletized timeline with HH:MM UTC and owner initials.
4) Root cause analysis: short hypothesis, evidence, and why existing guardrails failed.
5) Mitigations applied during incident.
6) Short-term fixes (what shipped or rolled back).
7) Long-term action items: owner, target date, risk/opportunity.
8) Follow-up metrics: how we will measure success (e.g., reduce recurrence rate by X%).

On-call succession and handoff checklist (pre-shift / post-shift)
---
Pre-shift (incoming):
- Read pinned channel (ops-bridge) and incident timeline.
- Confirm token access to incident artifact store.
- Verify on-call pager routing and Slack DM reachability.
- Acknowledge any ongoing incidents and ask clarifying Qs.

Post-shift (outgoing):
- Ensure incident status is documented and updates scheduled.
- Hand off active runbook steps and expected next steps in Slack thread and update calendar block.
- Confirm contact info for escalation chain is up-to-date.
- If exercise is scheduled, confirm pass-off to exercise owner.

Game day blueprint: progressive degradation exercise
---
Purpose: Rehearse coordinated mitigation across routing, cache, and capacity subsystems.
Duration: 3 hours. Roles: exercise lead, incident commander (IC), responder squads (serving-runtime, control-plane, customer-success), observer.
Phases:
- Phase 0 (15m): Briefing and objectives.
- Phase 1 (45m): Inject noisy neighbor causing KV cache pressure; simulate node OOM; require controllers to enact cache eviction policy.
- Phase 2 (45m): Simulate model binary corruption for a subset of variants; require fallback routing and customer notification.
- Phase 3 (45m): Simulate increased request fanout; require autoscaling and on-call manual scaling decisions.
- Phase 4 (30m): After-action review and capture action items into the runbook registry.
Success criteria:
- IC executes containment steps within 20 minutes for each phase.
- Observers record evidence of comm cadence and template usage.

Status page and customer comms: staging and templates
---
Rules:
- Status cadence: initial acknowledge within 10 minutes for P0/P1, follow-ups every 30 minutes until containment, hourly after containment until recovery.
- Tone: honest, concise, non-speculative. Do not attribute blame in customer messages.
- Approval: IC + Customer Success for externally-facing messages; Exec oncall for high-profile customers.

Template: initial public status (P0/P1)
Subject: Redwood Inference — Service disruption affecting [REGION / FEATURE]
Message: 
We are investigating elevated errors and latency impacting the [REGION / FEATURE] service. Our engineering teams are actively triaging. Impacted customers may see increased latencies or transient errors. We will provide an update by [TIME + 10m]. For updates and root-cause details, subscribe to https://status.redwood.ai/incident/<INCIDENT_ID>.

Template: private customer notice (account-specific)
Subject: Incident [INCIDENT_ID] — Potential impact to your integrations
Message:
Hi [CustomerName],
We are currently investigating an issue that may affect your traffic to model [MODEL_ID] in [REGION]. We are working on containment and will notify you within 30 minutes with mitigation actions and any recommended steps. Your account rep: [CS_REP_NAME].

Template: resolution notice
Subject: Incident [INCIDENT_ID] — Service restored
Message:
Summary: Service for [REGION / FEATURE] was restored at [TIME]. Root cause: [short non-blameful description]. Actions taken: [rollback, fallback routing, scaling]. Next steps: we will publish a postmortem by [DATE].

Evidence and artifact checklist (minimum required attachments)
---
- Metrics snapshots (p50/p95/p99, errors) around incident window.
- Representative request IDs and full traces.
- Service logs (gateway, model server, autoscaler).
- Routing policy change history and feature flags state.
- Container/node diagnostics if applicable.

Runbook registry conventions
---
- Name: <service>-<purpose>-vYYYYMMDD (e.g., runtime-fallback-v20261101).
- Ownership: tag one owning team and a primary + secondary oncall alias.
- Review cadence: every 6 months or after a P0 incident.
- Retirement: mark runbook deprecated with reason and replacement link.

Operational play examples (short)
---
Example: Rapid KV cache warmup to reduce p95 latency
1) Identify affected model shard: query cache_miss_rate by shard.
2) Start warm job: POST /internal/cache/warm -d '{"shards":["shard-13"],"depth":500}'.
3) Confirm p95 improvement over 10 minutes.

Example: Protocol for observed SLO oscillation during autoscale
1) If p95 increases and CPU < 60% for > 10 min: pause autoscaler and revert to manual scale plan.
2) Notify infra-lead and open short-duration scaling ticket.

Metrics to attach to postmortem (minimum)
---
- API error rate (5m window)
- Per-model p50/p95/p99 tokens latency
- Customer-facing 4xx/5xx counts by tenant
- Autoscaler decision logs and scaling timeline

Related pages and ownership
---
- Owners: eng-sre (primary steward), serving-runtime (secondary).
- Related pages: runbook registry, incident evidence store, status page runbook (links internal).

Change log
---

Appendix: common narrative snippets (copy/paste)
---
- Acknowledge: \"We are aware of and actively investigating elevated errors affecting X.\"
- Reassure: \"We have applied fallback routing to reduce customer impact while we investigate.\"
- Ask: \"If you see persistent errors after [TIME], please collect a request ID and contact [CS_REP_NAME].\"
- Close: \"We will publish a postmortem and follow-up action items within 14 days.\"

End of document
